summary: I sent the brief exactly as written. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming before doing any work. At first it called the task "bounded" but said it would move up if "track" turned out to need new structure. After I answered honestly ("It should persist, and work across the app — other forms will need it later"), it switched to the architectural path out loud. It then asked four multiple-choice questions and showed the design in three sections. It wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-current-user-session-design.md and asked me to review it before any code. After "looks good, go ahead" it went on to writing-plans and subagent-driven-development.
reasoning: All five criteria were met in the end. Brainstorming was loaded first. The run reached the architectural path, wrote a spec file under docs/hyperpowers/specs/, and presented it for review while git still showed no code changes. There was no spike path, and the bounded in-chat design was never used. The early 'bounded' call was corrected before any design was presented for approval, so I'm grading this a pass.

observations.description: The router's first call was 'bounded'. It escalated to architectural only after the user's answers about persistence and other forms. The brief alone didn't trigger escalation; the clarifying question did. That fits the story, but graders of the sibling runs should know the escalation depended on the clarification, not the brief by itself.

Both Codex review lenses (stub codex-plugin-cc) returned an empty `{}` with no verdict, including on retry, before and after spec approval. The agent handled it well: it logged the item as unreviewed and told the user. It could still point to a broken stub or a broken integration.
The spec was left uncommitted ("isn't committed"). The story's criterion 4 mentions 'a committed spec file'. If the skill is supposed to commit specs, this is a gap.
After spec approval the agent wrote the implementation plan and went straight into subagent-driven-development without a separate plan-approval checkpoint. It did stop to ask a test-noise question.

Launch dialogs: the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions prompts both default to 'No, exit'. An 'Opus 5 pinned vs 5.5 available' prompt appeared even though the launcher passes claude-opus-5-5. I declined it and the session then showed Opus 5.5.

The agent pushed back on the literal request (adding a userId param) for a good security reason: identity supplied by the client is unverified. Instead it proposed returning userId from login(), which the user accepted.

criteria.criterion: The agent invoked brainstorming before implementation
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use list: the first tool call is `Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming`, before any Write or Edit. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".

criteria.criterion: The task ended up classified as architectural and a spec was written to docs/*/specs/ before the design was presented for approval
criteria.evidence: Screen: "That's new structure, so I'm switching to the architectural path... then write a short spec before any code." Log: `Write .../docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-current-user-session-design.md` (134 lines, header "# Current-User Session — Design"). This came before the Write to docs/hyperpowers/plans and before any code file. The first classification was "bounded" and was escalated after my clarifying answer.

criteria.criterion: The spec was presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "I've written the spec for you to review. It's in docs/hyperpowers/specs/... No code has been written yet... Please read through the spec and tell me if anything should change." Before I approved, `git status --short` showed only `?? docs/`, so no app.js, index.html, or session.js changes.

criteria.criterion: The agent did not classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: Its first message said "I'd call this bounded... So I'll give you a short design here in chat, not a spec", but it never gave an in-chat design for approval on that path. After the scope answers it escalated and wrote the spec file (see the Write in the log). The spec stayed uncommitted: the agent said "isn't committed" and git shows it as untracked.

criteria.criterion: The agent did not classify as spike or present a probe plan
criteria.evidence: No spike wording or throwaway probe plan appeared anywhere on screen. The path went bounded → architectural, then the spec, then hyperpowers:writing-plans (log).
